questions.stem: A 30-year-old man presented with a 1-week history of a painful right eye with blurry vision and photophobia. He wore contact lenses and had been using tap water to clean them. On eye examination, a corneal ulcer was identified. Investigations: Microscopy of corneal scrapings: amebic cysts and trophozoites seen
questions.lead_in: What is the most likely agent?
questions.explanation: Acanthamoeba sp. This is a case of Acanthamoeba keratitis associated with improper contact lens care. Entamoeba histolytica is an amoebic parasite but would be very unusual as a cause of keratitis. Giardia lamblia is a flagellate protozoan and not known to cause keratitis. Balamuthia is a free-living ameba similar to Acanthamoeba but typically causes CNS or cutaneous disease and not keratitis. Dientamoeba is only associated with GI disease.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 4 Q34

questions.question: A man has keratitis; eye cultures are negative for bacteria, fungi, and mycobacteria.
questions.question_raw:
Q30 (2007)
Man with keratitis and eye cultures negative for bacteria, fungi, and mycobacteria.

parts.text: Two risk factors for this condition

parts_raw.text: B) 2 risk factors for this condition

questions.model_answer:
a) Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1) keratitis - culture-negative dendritic/geographic epithelial keratitis with reduced corneal sensation (present in ~70%). (Considered: adenoviral keratoconjunctivitis, varicella-zoster/HZO keratitis, Acanthamoeba - all also culture-negative on routine media.)

b) (1) Topical or systemic corticosteroid or immunosuppressive drug use, and immunodeficiency states (malignancy, organ transplant). (2) Prior ocular HSV infection/latent trigeminal infection - recurrence rate ~40% over 5 years; also trauma or corneal epithelial disruption (including contact lens wear).

c) (1) Long-term suppressive oral antiviral prophylaxis: acyclovir 400 mg PO BID - HEDS II showed 45% reduction in recurrence (19% vs 32% at 1 year, P < .001). (2) Avoid unopposed corticosteroids/immunosuppressives - never give topical steroids for HSV keratitis without concurrent antiviral cover, since steroids without antiviral prophylaxis allow rapid geographic ulceration.

cohort_answer.text:
A) HSV. DDx: Adenovirus (more often causes conjunctivitis, but some strains can cause keratoconjunctivitis).

B) Use of immunosuppressants or immunodeficiency; location of HSV lesions.

C) Suppressive oral antivirals with valacyclovir or acyclovir (25-50% have recurrence within 2 years); avoid immunosuppressants.
